title: Ecommerce Website
summary: Full-stack online store with a backend-driven catalog, cart and orders, OAuth login and an AI shopping assistant.
description: A mock ecommerce platform I built to get hands-on with full-stack development. It covers the basics you'd expect from an online store: products, a shopping cart and order handling.

I kept the frontend thin and let the backend do the heavy lifting, so product management and the cart logic all live server-side. I also added OAuth login to understand how real-world auth flows work, plus a small AI chatbot that helps users find products.

title: Vault
summary: Personal budgeting app: set a monthly budget, log expenses and see where the money actually goes.
description: A personal budgeting app built to take control of your finances. You set up a monthly budget, track expenses as they happen, and get a clear picture of where your money is going.
The goal was to make budgeting feel less like a chore, so the focus was on a clean interface and data that's easy to read at a glance.

title: Task App
summary: React Native task manager with its own backend, built to learn how mobile clients talk to an API.
description: A task manager I built as part of my Personal Development Plan to get into mobile development. I went with React Native so I could learn how a mobile app connects to a backend.
You can add tasks, mark them done, and view your week at a glance. Everything is persisted server-side, so tasks survive between sessions and devices.

title: Smart Time Registration
summary: Imports Outlook calendars and automatically links meetings to projects, so nobody has to log hours by hand.
description: A time-tracking tool that takes the hassle out of logging hours. Instead of entering everything manually, you import your Outlook calendar and the app links meetings and events to the right projects.
We integrated Microsoft authentication so organisations can roll it out securely. The idea came from seeing how much time people waste just tracking their time. Built with a team at university.

images.caption: Home page with imported calendar data

title: StreamFlix
summary: Backend for a streaming platform: user accounts, auth, watchlists and content served through a REST API.
description: A Netflix-style streaming platform built to dig into backend development. It handles user accounts, lets users build a watchlist, and serves content through a proper API.
I wanted to understand how streaming services work behind the scenes: authentication, managing user data, and keeping track of what people want to watch. The backend was the main focus.

title: Bin There, Done That
summary: Teaches kids to recycle through sorting mini-games, with AI that identifies what kind of waste something is.
description: An educational web app that teaches kids about recycling through mini-games. We wanted waste separation to actually be fun, so players sort trash into the right bins in a set of interactive games.
There's also an AI feature that identifies what type of waste an item is. Simple, colourful, and built so the lesson sticks. A group project focused on making sustainability education more engaging.

title: NHL Stenden Explorer
summary: Virtual tour of the Emmen campus with 360° photos we shot ourselves, plus an FAQ for visitors.
description: A virtual campus tour for NHL Stenden's Emmen campus, so students, staff, parents and visitors can explore it without being there.

The core is a 360° photo viewer: we walked the campus with a 360 camera and integrated the shots so you can look around as if you're standing there. An FAQ section covers what people usually want to know about the facilities. Built with a team.

title: SSM Product Passport
summary: A digital passport that follows a product through the supply chain: origin, sustainability data and history.
description: A product tracking system built for a university group project. The idea is a 'passport' for products: a digital record that follows an item through the supply chain.

You can see where a product came from, check its sustainability credentials, and trace where it's been. We used UNS-inspired data principles to keep everything structured and traceable, so manufacturers, suppliers and customers can all verify details from one place.
